title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed English text, numbered p. 85, with handwritten formulas. It looks like a translated lecture course on algebraic surfaces, plausibly in the style of Shafarevich's lectures on minimal models and contraction of exceptional curves, though I have not verified the source. Grothendieck may have filed it for reference.

Setting: V is a (nonsingular, projective) surface and E' is a divisor, presumably a configuration of exceptional curves. [D] denotes twisting by the line bundle of the divisor D. 𝓔'_ν denotes the ν-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of E', or some subscheme supported on E' that contains it. The inclusion O_V(-νE') ⊂ O_V(-𝓔'_ν) of ideal sheaves has a coherent quotient G supported on E'.

Step 1, inequality (21). By an observation made earlier in the proof, H^1(V, G[nE']) = 0 for n large. This is presumably a vanishing for sheaves supported on E' after twisting by a line bundle that is positive in the relevant sense. Twist the sequence 0 → O_V(-νE') → O_V(-𝓔'_ν) → G → 0 by nE' and take the long exact cohomology sequence. The map H^1(O_V[(n-ν)E']) → H^1(O_V(-𝓔'_ν)[nE']) is then surjective, which gives (21).

Step 2, inequality (22). Twist 0 → O_V(-𝓔'_ν) → O_V → O_{𝓔'_ν} → 0 by nE'. Use H^1(O_{𝓔'_ν}[nE']) = 0 for n ≥ n(𝓔'_ν). Then H^1(O_V(-𝓔'_ν)[nE']) → H^1(O_V[nE']) is surjective, which gives (22).

Combining the two: dim H^1(V, O_V[nE']) ≤ dim H^1(V, O_V[(n-ν)E']) for n large. Hence dim H^1(O_V[nE']) is bounded and eventually non-increasing. This is the standard step in proving the contractibility criterion for curves with negative-definite intersection matrix (Grauert, Artin), or the finite generation and normality arguments that come with it.
errors: The middle sequence is typed as 0 → O_V(-𝓔'_ν) → O_V → O_{E'} → 0. The quotient should be O_{𝓔'_ν}, not O_{E'}, since the kernel is the ideal of 𝓔'_ν.
The inequality (21) is typed twice, once numbered and once after 'or'. The second line was probably meant as a rewritten form, e.g. using O_V(-νE')[nE'] = O_V[(n-ν)E'], and adds nothing.

The vanishing H^1(G[nE']) = 0 for large n relies on an 'observation from the beginning of the proof' that is not on this page. Whether it holds depends on the sign convention for [nE'] relative to the negativity of E'; it cannot be checked here.

ideas.what: Bounding h^1 of O_V(nE') via infinitesimal neighbourhoods of an exceptional configuration, using two short exact sequences and vanishing on sheaves supported on the curve
ideas.modern_name: Cohomological step in the Grauert/Artin contractibility criterion; formal-neighbourhood estimates
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grauert (1962), M. Artin (1962); Zariski; textbook form in Shafarevich's lectures on minimal models (1966)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed page from someone else's text, apparently an English translation of lectures on surfaces and contraction of curves. The argument is a routine long-exact-sequence estimate. It contains no Grothendieck mathematics and nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The quotient in the second exact sequence appears in the image as O_{E'} (subscript E', possibly with the ν dropped). Mathematically it should be O_{𝓔'_ν}.
In the second, unnumbered inequality the bracket is handwritten as something like 'O_V[(n-ν)E']'. The parentheses are garbled in the image but mean the same as in (21).
The faint pencil mark '114' at the bottom left is an archive folio number. The page's own number is 85.
